newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says will launch locally-built submarine.
newsitem.headline: Iran says will launch locally-built submarine.

text.p: Iran will soon launch its first locally-built submarine to boost its navy, which already has Russian-built submarines, an Iranian military official said in remarks published on Wednesday.

"The Iranian-built submarine is being used experimentally now and has research facilities" Navy Commodore Mohammad Reza Rahmati told the newspaper Iran. "It will be commissioned soon after being equipped with military facilities."
Rahmati, who is deputy head of the navy's logistics department, gave no further details. Iran has said earlier that it was building a small submarine.
Western naval sources on Tuesday confirmed an Iranian report that Iran would soon receive a third Russian diesel submarine.
Tehran radio said a fighter plane on Wednesday for the first time fired an air-to-sea missile named Piroozi (Victory)-75 during a major military exercise in the Gulf.

It said the missile had a range of 90 miles (145 km) and could withstand electronic jamming. Iranian media earlier said it was an updated version of the Silkworm missile, suggesting Iranian technicians had improved the Chinese-made missile.
Some 100 ships, including destroyers, gunboats, hovercraft and Iran's two existing Russian-built submarines were taking part in the exercise, backed by 40 planes and helicopters.
A locally-built rocket launcher named Tondar (Thunder) was also tested, a navy official told Iran's news agency IRNA.
The Tondar was "totally designed by Iranian experts and manufactured based on advanced systems such as mobile defence and electronic warfare systems", the official added.

The London-based Jane's Defence Weekly said in May it had received reports that Iran was building a ballistic missile named Tondar-68 with a range of 700 km (440 miles) which it said was built with Chinese and North Korean help.
It said the Tondar was possibly a modified Chinese C-801 Sardine anti-ship missile, or the more advanced C-802 missile.
Iran has denied co-operating with North Korea on building missiles. Tehran on Saturday also dismissed as baseless a report that it recently purchased missile technology from China.
Washington and its Gulf Arab allies have expressed concern over Iran's armaments programme. Tehran says its military programme is purely defensive.
